meta.note: Fossil reference layer: curated worldwide groups (incl. trace fossils, petrified wood, pseudofossils) with Texas formations, plus PBDB genera (Texas, >=3 occurrences, and a worldwide list). Facts and links only; not identifications.

sources.name: UT BEG Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Ammonites (coiled ammonoids)
types.dates: ~410-66 Ma; formations: Eagle Ford (102.66-88.78 Ma), Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma), Del Rio (101.96-95.55 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma), Duck Creek (113.2-95.55 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Shell coiled flat in one plane, divided into chambers; complex frilly suture lines where the septa meet the outer wall. Texas has many Cretaceous genera.

sources.name: UT Bureau of Economic Geology, Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Baculites (straight ammonites)
types.dates: ~95-66 Ma; formations: Taylor (82.17-66.0 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
similar_types: crinoid stems (round, with a central hole)
lookalikes: crinoid stems (round, with a central hole)
types.diagnostic: Straight, slightly tapering shell with an oval cross-section and frilly suture lines; often broken into segments.

types.name: Brachiopods (lamp shells)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
formations: Pennsylvanian and Permian of North and West Texas
types.diagnostic: Two unequal valves (top and bottom), each symmetrical left-to-right; a beak with a pedicle opening. Abundant in Texas Paleozoic rocks.

types.name: Bryozoans (moss animals)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Colonies of tiny (<1 mm) pores, forming lacy fans, twigs or crusts; Archimedes has a screw-shaped axis.

types.name: Clams and other bivalves
types.dates: ~520 Ma-present; formations: Weches (42.79-40.48 Ma), Reklaw (50.05-46.31 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Two valves that are mirror images of each other (left/right), usually asymmetrical front-to-back; hinge with teeth; often preserved as internal molds (steinkerns).

types.name: Coprolites (fossil dung)
types.dates: ~420 Ma-present; formations: Eagle Ford (102.66-88.78 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Elongate dense phosphatic masses, sometimes with fish scales or bone bits inside.

types.name: Corals (solitary and colonial)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Cups (corallites) with radiating vertical plates (septa); colonial corals look like honeycomb or bundles of tubes.

types.name: Crinoids (sea lilies): stems and columnals
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Small discs (columnals) with a central canal, stacked into stems; Paleozoic limestones are often made of crinoid debris.

types.name: Exogyra / Ilymatogyra (coiled oysters)
types.dates: ~125-66 Ma; formations: Del Rio (101.96-95.55 Ma), Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma), Taylor (82.17-66.0 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Thick, heavy left valve with a beak that curls sideways (spiral, like a ram's horn); flat lid valve; concentric growth lamellae. Common in Texas Upper Cretaceous marls and chalks.

sources.name: UT Bureau of Economic Geology, Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Gryphaea / Texigryphaea (cup oysters)
types.dates: ~200-66 Ma; formations: Walnut (113.2-100.5 Ma), Goodland (143.1-100.5 Ma), Duck Creek (113.2-95.55 Ma), Fort Worth (103.55-101.77 Ma), Grayson (100.5-96.38 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Deep cup-shaped valve with a beak curving over the hinge (not sideways), small flat lid. Abundant in Lower Cretaceous Washita/Fredericksburg rocks of North-Central Texas.

sources.name: UT Bureau of Economic Geology, Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Inoceramus (inoceramid clams)
types.dates: ~200-66 Ma; formations: Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma), Eagle Ford (102.66-88.78 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Large thin-shelled clams with strong concentric folds; broken shell shows prismatic (fibrous) calcite edges.

sources.name: UT Bureau of Economic Geology, Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Leaf and plant impressions
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Flat carbon films or impressions with a midrib and vein network.

types.name: Microfossils and shell-hash limestone (forams, ostracods)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Rock made largely of tiny shells; needs a hand lens. The Austin Chalk is mostly coccoliths and forams.

types.name: Nautiloids
types.dates: ~500 Ma-present; formations: Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma), Weches (42.79-40.48 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Chambered shell with simple, gently curved suture lines and a central siphuncle; coiled or straight (orthocones).

types.name: Oysters and oyster shell hash (Ostreidae and relatives)
types.dates: ~250 Ma-present; formations: Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma), Taylor (82.17-66.0 Ma), Midway (66.0-54.02 Ma), Weches (42.79-40.48 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Irregular, layered shells cemented to each other or to a surface; concentrated beds form 'shell hash' limestone.

types.name: Petrified (silicified) wood
types.dates: ~390-2.6 Ma; formations: Wilcox (64.92-33.9 Ma), Jackson (37.71-10.08 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
formations: Nevada Miocene (e.g. Virgin Valley, Hubbard Basin)
types.diagnostic: Wood replaced by silica: lengthwise grain, end-grain growth rings and rays, shrinkage checks across the grain. Texas: Catahoula and other Paleogene-Neogene units. Nevada is famous for Miocene opalized and agatized wood.

types.name: Pseudofossil: concretions, septarian nodules and iron nodules
types.dates: any age; formations: Eagle Ford (102.66-88.78 Ma), Taylor (82.17-66.0 Ma), Wilcox (64.92-33.9 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Hard masses cemented around a nucleus, often round or knobby, sometimes with crack fillings (septarian). Lack internal anatomy (no bone texture, no septa, no growth lines). The most common 'fossil' lookalike.

types.name: Pseudofossil: manganese dendrites
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Black, fern-like mineral crystals (manganese oxides) on rock surfaces and fractures; branch pattern has no midrib or cell structure. Not a fossil.

types.name: Pseudofossil: weathering pits, chert knobs and dissolution shapes
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Pits, cups and knobs left where softer parts weather out of limestone or chert; the pattern is random and lacks repeated anatomical structure.

types.name: Sea urchins (echinoids), incl. heart urchins
types.dates: ~450 Ma-present; formations: Glen Rose (113.2-100.5 Ma), Walnut (113.2-100.5 Ma), Del Rio (101.96-95.55 Ma), Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Rounded test with five-fold (pentaradial) symmetry: five petal-like ambulacral bands; heart urchins have a groove at the front.

sources.name: UT Bureau of Economic Geology, Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Shark and ray teeth
types.dates: ~400 Ma-present; formations: Eagle Ford (102.66-88.78 Ma), Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma), Kemp (67.55-67.05 Ma), Weches (42.79-40.48 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
similar_types: chert flakes and small points (no root, no enamel)
lookalikes: chert flakes and small points (no root, no enamel)
types.diagnostic: Glossy enamel crown on a two-lobed bony root; Ptychodus teeth are flat crushing plates with ridges. Abundant in Texas Cretaceous chalks and Eocene greensands.

sources.name: UT Bureau of Economic Geology, Geologic Atlas of Texas

types.name: Snails (gastropods), incl. Turritella
types.dates: ~520 Ma-present; formations: Weches (42.79-40.48 Ma), Glen Rose (113.2-100.5 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Single shell coiled in a helical (3-D) spiral around an axis, no internal chambers or suture lines; Turritella is tall and screw-like.

types.name: Sponges (Porifera), incl. silicified sponges
types.dates: ~540 Ma-present; formations: Glen Rose (113.2-100.5 Ma), Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Cup, ball or vase shapes with pores, canals and one or more larger openings (oscula); no radial septa. Often silicified, which makes them easy to confuse with chert nodules.

types.name: Trace fossils: burrows (Thalassinoides, Ophiomorpha)
types.dates: ~540 Ma-present; formations: Austin (89.8-75.05 Ma), Eagle Ford (102.66-88.78 Ma), Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Cylindrical tubes or branching networks made by animals; Ophiomorpha tubes have a pelleted, knobby outer wall. Flint nodules in chalk often fill Thalassinoides burrows.

types.name: Trace fossils: tracks and trails (incl. dinosaur tracks)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Impressions left by moving animals; dinosaur tracks in the Glen Rose Formation are world-famous.

types.name: Trilobites
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Segmented body divided lengthwise into three lobes, with a head shield (cephalon) and tail shield (pygidium).

types.name: Vertebrate bone and teeth (fish, reptiles, mammals)
types.dates: ~480 Ma-present; formations: Navarro (75.05-66.0 Ma), Taylor (82.17-66.0 Ma)
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Bone shows a spongy (cancellous) interior with a denser outer layer and often sticks to the tongue; teeth have enamel. Pleistocene terrace gravels can carry mammoth, horse and bison.

types.name: Belemnites
types.region_notes: Worldwide group; Texas formations listed where known
types.diagnostic: Solid bullet-shaped calcite 'guard' with radiating fibrous structure in cross-section; rare in Texas, common in Europe.
